thread:
Alex W.: quick sync — during the continuous-batcher stress run I started seeing OOM kills when batches include long-prefix requests that touch large KV spans. reproducer: `tests/perf/batch_kv_stress.py --workers=8 --max-seqlen=2048`
Priya S.: ugh, saw that too. profiler shows a big jump in GPU memory at the moment the batch forms (not token generation). looks like kv materialization for multiple sequences happens before trimming.
Dan L.: do we have numbers? peak memory vs baseline?
Alex W.: baseline steady state ~28.3 GB, spike to ~41.7 GB right when batch assembled (on a 48GB card) — that's why OOMs cropped up on smaller instances. attached flame showed `kv_materialize` and `kv_copy_async` dominating.
Marta: that matches my run. Also noticed kernel selection shifts to a slower kernel when seqlens in batch are heterogeneous — increases temporary buffer requirements.
Kai: idea — impose a cache-aware batch token budget: at batch formation time compute estimated_kv_bytes = sum(estimated_kv_per_token * left_prefix_tokens) and reject or defer requests if estimated_kv_bytes + current_kv_mem > kv_mem_threshold. simple gate before forming.
Priya S.: +1. we need something low-cost to compute. we can use per-customer avg_kv_per_token and approximate left_prefix_tokens from request metadata (we already store cached prefix lengths).
Dan L.: we also need fairness — don't starve small requests. propose a queue policy: 1) fast lane for requests with estimated_kv_bytes < small_thresh, 2) priority bucketing with token_budget windows that replenish every 100ms.
Alex W.: sketch pseudocode I tried last night:
```
if estimated_kv_bytes + current_kv_mem > kv_mem_limit:
  if request.tokens <= small_token_threshold:
    put_in_fast_lane(request)
  else:
    delay(request, backoff=calc_backoff(queued_bytes))
else:
  include_in_batch(request)
```
Kai: that looks reasonable. what about kernel selection side effects? if we force more homogeneous seqlen batches we might get the faster kernel more often. maybe add a heuristic to avoid mixing >2x seqlen ratio.
Marta: profiling from last week shows 18-22% latency regression when heterogeneous batches trigger fallback kernel. making seqlen-homogeneity constraint could reduce OOM but increase latency for some flows — tradeoff.
Priya S.: ops-bot just posted one of the OOM alerts earlier:
```
ops-bot: [alert] worker-23 OOM killed (reason: CUDA OOM) pid=18204 model=redwood-v4 batch_size=12 seqlens=[192,1024,150,2048,64,512,300,128,900,30,60,200]
```
Dan L.: that seqlen mix is brutal. we should simulate that distribution in the perf harness and measure both memory and p50/p99.
Alex W.: agreed. next actions: 1) Priya & Dan to implement lightweight estimated_kv_bytes calc and gate in the batcher (safe default to only delay non-small requests). 2) Kai & Marta to add seqlen-homogeneity score and a tunable threshold + perf runs. 3) I'll add regression tests in CI with the reproducer and one synthetic trace that caused the OOM.
Priya S.: I'll open a minimal PR with the gate and a flag `--kv-gate-enabled` and instrument metrics: `kv_est_bytes`, `batch_blocked_reasons`.
Kai: good. also add a metric for `kernel_fallback_rate` when batch heterogeneity triggers slower kernel. helps tune the tradeoff.
Marta: FYI, I think we should cap the number of prefixes materialized per-batch simultaneously (eg max_prefixes=8) as an extra safety net. small clients won't be affected.
Alex W.: sounds good. set owner Alex/ Priya/ Kai. We'll try to land changes behind feature flags and run e2e perf in a canary pool.
Priya S.: ETA for PR by EOD tomorrow. I'll include a tiny repro script and the perf numbers. :thumbsup:
Dan L.: I'll add the perf harness scenarios.
ops-bot: scheduled perf job `batcher-kv-gate-canary` queued (run-id=8742).
